Basic Setup and Simulation Quality Settings This section covers initializing a simple garment model in CLO, adjusting simulation parameters for optimal balance between quality and speed, and preparing the animation environment. - **Starting the Project**: Load a basic outfit composed of two garment pieces. - **Quality Settings**: - Default board size: 5 - Thickness: 1 - Model surface diameter: 0 (can be adjusted based on needs) - **Simulation Speed vs. Quality**: - High-quality simulation uses a board size of 510 (default 5 and thickness 1 scaled). - High-quality simulation slows down the dynamic simulation process. - Before recording animation, reduce particle diameter (e.g., to 20) and increase conflict thickness (default 2.5) to prevent garment layer collisions and penetrations. - **Animation Mode**: - Switch to animation mode from the main interface’s upper right corner. - Use "Animation Completion" setting to increase simulation iterations from 1 to 5 for more accurate cloth behavior, sacrificing speed for stability. --- ## 2. Animation and Motion Application This section explains how to add model motions, transition actions, and record garment simulations. - **Adding Motions**: - Use preset folders (e.g., V2 folder in version 5.2) containing motion files. - Double-click a motion file to import an action; always enable "transition into first position" for smooth movement and garment-model synchronization. - **Action Bar and Progress**: - Use the action progress bar to preview and fine-tune animation sequences. - Always reset to the starting position after testing an action to maintain garment-model alignment. - **Recording Simulation**: - Enable recording button to start simulation capturing dynamic garment behavior during model motion. - The system records the entire dynamic cloth process on a progress bar. - **Common Issues**: - If collars or garment parts overstretch or deform excessively during animation, adjust elasticity and use fixing tools to stabilize. --- ## 3. Garment Stability and Adjustment Techniques This section details methods to ensure garments behave realistically and remain stable during animations. - **Collar Elasticity Adjustment**: - Select collar lines and increase elasticity ratio from default 80% to 100% to prevent overstretching. - **Fixing Points (Armor Tool)**: - Use the Armor tool to fix garment points to the model. - Left-click to assign a fixed point on the garment and corresponding point on the model, preventing unwanted movement. - **Model Position Reset**: - Right-click model and select "Move virtual model clothing to center" to reset model alignment. - **Simulation Optimization**: - Use low-quality simulation (larger particle size) for quick previews. - Switch back to high-quality (smaller particle size, but keep conflict thickness) for final recordings. - **Playback Settings**: - Adjust playback speed and enable loop playback. - Set playback start and end points using the blue progress bar. - Time axis ratio can be adjusted to slow down or speed up simulation for stability in complex animations. --- ## 4. Multi-layer Garments and Grouping This section explains handling complex outfits with multiple layers, such as jackets, shirts, and pants. - **Grouping Function** (introduced in version 5.2): - Group multiple garment pieces for easier selection and manipulation. - **Layer Freezing**: - Freeze garments that are not currently being adjusted to speed up simulation and avoid unwanted interactions. - **Conflict Management for Buttons and Overlapping Parts**: - Turn off conflict on buttons and overlapping parts via the twist editor tool to prevent simulation errors. - **Grid Tool for Adjustments**: - Use the grid tool to adjust garment pieces quickly, ensuring proper fit and preventing fabric penetration. - **Shrink Rate Adjustment**: - Adjust “微向缩率” (micro shrink rate) to tighten garment edges and prevent fabric from protruding. - **Conflict Thickness**: - Increase conflict thickness between layers to avoid fabric collision and penetration, typically set between 2.5 to 3. --- ## 5. Reducing Complexity for Performance To improve simulation speed and stability in complex garments: - Delete internal or hidden fabric pieces that are not visible during the show to reduce computational load. - Simplify complex structures such as multi-layered sleeves or heavy suits. - Use freezing strategically to isolate and stabilize specific garment layers. --- ## 6. Accessory Integration: Bags, Belts, Metal Rings This section covers how to add and simulate accessories on garments. - **Bags**: - Use default fabric presets optimized for leather or hard materials. - Increase bending strength to keep bag shape stable during motion. - Fix bag position with pins or fixing needles so it moves naturally but does not slip or fall. - Adjust pin length (e.g., 1-2 mm) to maintain slight gaps for natural movement. - **Belts and Metal Rings**: - Do not import metal buckles as virtual models; import them as copies (OBJ format) to follow garment movement without collision simulation. - Create a hidden small panel to fix metal parts inside the garment. - Use fold tools to create holes or creases for rings to fit naturally. - Import rings as OBJ files, set material to metal, and position them with watering tool for stability. - Avoid layering conflicts by strategic placement and fixing. --- ## 7. Headwear and Hair Integration Handling hats, headscarves, and hairstyles in animations. - **Hats**: - Complex hats with multiple parts (face, inside) should be imported as OBJ and attached as copies. - Stick hats to the top of the model’s head by creating a small board on the head and fixing it with needles. - Adjust hat position carefully to avoid clipping with hair. - Use short hairstyles or remove hair meshes under hats for better fit. - **Hair**: - Hair can be fixed similarly by adding multiple fixing points alternating along the mesh to reduce deformation. - For simpler operations, hair can also be converted to OBJ and pinned. - **Animation**: - Once fixed, hats and hair follow the model movement naturally during walk animations. --- ## 8. Earrings and Small Accessories - Earrings and other small accessories generally use reverse layering to speed up simulation when no level conflict exists. - Simplify accessories by reducing complexity or removing unnecessary geometry. - Fix accessories similarly to hats and rings to prevent unwanted movement or collisions. --- ## 9. Stage Setup for Walk Shows - CLO provides pre-set stage project files (DPRJ format) in the library. - Import stage files before starting walk show animations to avoid losing actions. - Stages can be added to the work area by right-click or double-click. - Customize environment elements like grids and lighting for presentation. - Use animation mode to record walk and accessory animations with stage. --- ## 10. Exporting and Playback of Recorded Shows - Recorded shows are saved in AVR format for interactive playback. - If customer’s playback does not support AVR, convert using video editing software to MP4. - Playback speed and loop options can be adjusted. - Video capture feature allows exporting walk shows as video files without rendering. - Full rendering with lighting takes longer and is optional. --- ## 11. Additional Tips and Troubleshooting - **Model and Motion Compatibility**: - CLO version 5.2 supports both V1 and V2 models with motions. - Older versions only support V1 motions. - **Model Reset**: - Use right-click option to move virtual model clothing to center if off-position. - **Simulation Speed vs. Quality**: - Balance particle size and conflict thickness to maintain simulation speed without sacrificing stability. - **Fixing Unstable Garments**: - Use fixing needles and pins extensively on collars, sleeves, and bag attachments. - Avoid excessive conflict layers which increase instability. - **Importing External Motions** (e.g., Mixamo): - Upload FBX files with textures preserved. - CLO supports FBX imports for motions; refer to official forum articles for detailed workflows. - **Color and Material Tips**: - Avoid overly bright or pure white colors for better texture reflection. - Use water-based colors for fabric samples. - **Use of Shortcuts**: - Shift + Q to hide clothing pieces. - Shift + W to show hidden clothing pieces. --- This guide consolidates key techniques for preparing and presenting 3D garment walk shows in CLO, covering garment simulation, animation, accessory integration, and stage setup with best practices to optimize performance and visual fidelity.
